title: Degree-zero resolution base change equals ordinary module base change
statement: Let f:X→S and g:S′→S be morphisms of schemes with g flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Put Z=S′×_S X, q=pullback.snd g f and p=pullback.fst g f [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let F be an O_X-module, I an injective resolution of F and J an injective resolution of q^*F, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let t:I→q_*J be a cochain map with I.ι⁰ t⁰ = η_q,F q_*(J.ι⁰). Let beta⁰ be flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t 0 [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-construction] and B the ordinary moduleBaseChangeMap f p g q pullback.condition.symm F [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction]. Let ζ_f,F:f_*F→R⁰f_*F and ζ_p,q^*F:p_*q^*F→R⁰p_*q^*F be the canonical toRightDerivedZero maps. Then g^*(ζ_f,F) beta⁰ = B ζ_p,q^*F, with diagrammatic composition. No properness, quasi-coherence or flatness of q is assumed beyond the displayed data.

source.place: Lemma 20.17.1, augmentation diagram and termwise adjunction in its proof

proof.text: Write Q=f_*t followed by the pushforward-square comparison and C for its termwise g-adjoint, as in the resolution construction. Taking degree zero of the complex adjunction identity gives homEquiv_g(C⁰)=Q⁰. Apply homEquiv_g to g^*(f_*(I.ι⁰)) C⁰. Naturality on the left gives f_*(I.ι⁰) Q⁰. Substitute the augmentation equation for t and use naturality of the pushforward-square comparison on J.ι⁰. This equals homEquiv_g(B) g_*p_*(J.ι⁰). Naturality on the right and injectivity give g^*f_*(I.ι⁰) C⁰=B p_*(J.ι⁰).

Flat pullback preserves finite limits and colimits. For any short complex K, its mapHomologyIso and mapCyclesIso obey π_(g*K) mapHomologyIso.hom = mapCyclesIso.hom g^*(π_K). This follows by writing mapHomologyIso using LeftHomologyData.mapHomologyIso_eq and applying homologyπ_comp_homologyIso_hom and π_comp_homologyIso_inv. For the two pushed-forward resolution complexes, move the source augmentation across mapCyclesIso.inv and cyclesMap C. Postcomposition with the monic target iCycles reduces this to the component identity from the previous step. Then homologyπ_naturality gives the corresponding homology identity. These are the completely proved private helpers map_homologyπ and augmented_homology.

Mathlib InjectiveResolution.toRightDerivedZero_eq expresses each canonical ζ as toRightDerivedZero′, the degree-zero cycles-to-homology map, and the inverse resolution-computation isomorphism. Substitute these expressions and the definition of beta⁰. Cancel the image of the source resolution isomorphism and its inverse. The homology identity from the previous step, postcomposed with the inverse target resolution-computation isomorphism, is exactly the required equality.

lean.statement:
theorem flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta_degree_zero
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g]
    (F : X.Modules) (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj F))
    (t : I.cocomplex ⟶ ((pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj J.cocomplex)
    (ht : I.ι.f 0 ≫ t.f 0 =
      (Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd g f))).unit.app F ≫
        (pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).map (J.ι.f 0)) :
    (tensorPullback g).map ((pushforward f).toRightDerivedZero.app F) ≫
        flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t 0 =
      moduleBaseChangeMap f (pullback.fst g f) g (pullback.snd g f)
        pullback.condition.symm F ≫
          (pushforward (pullback.fst g f)).toRightDerivedZero.app
            ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj F)
